quotations.quote_markdown:
Next, let us write

$$h\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\log(q^{\forall})=\frac{1}{[F:\mathbb Q]}\cdot\sum_{v\in\mathbb V(F)^{\mathrm{non}}}h_v\cdot f_v\cdot\log(p_v)$$

— that is to say, $h_v=0$ for those $v$ at which $E_F$ has good reduction; $h_v\in\mathbb N_{\geq1}$ is the local height of $E_F$ [cf. [GenEll], Definition 3.3] for those $v$ at which $E_F$ has bad multiplicative reduction. Now it follows [by assertion (i); [GenEll], Proposition 1.4, (iv)] that the inequality $h^{1/2}<\xi_{\mathrm{prm}}$ [cf. the notation of Proposition 2.1, (ii)] implies that there is only a finite number of possibilities for the $j$-invariant of $E_F$. Thus, by possibly enlarging the finite set $\mathfrak{Exc}_d$ [in a fashion that depends only on $K_V$, $d$, and $\epsilon_d$ and in such a way that $h\leq H_{\mathrm{unif}}$ on $\mathfrak{Exc}_d$ for some positive real number $H_{\mathrm{unif}}$ that is independent of $K_V$], we may assume without loss of generality that the inequality

$$h^{1/2}\geq\xi_{\mathrm{prm}}\geq5$$

holds.

scope.en: Definition 3.3 identifies the local integer Tate order. The proof of Corollary 2.2(ii) sums these orders with the residue degree and the logarithm of the residue characteristic. The finite-height equality itself comes from the reference Lean theorem at Height.lean:582.
scope.zh-Hans: 定义 3.3 给出 Tate 参数的局部整数阶。推论 2.2（二）的证明用剩余次数及剩余标数的对数为权重，对这些局部阶求和。有限高度等式的直接出处是参考 Lean 工程 Height.lean 第 582 行。
scope.ja: 定義 3.3 は Tate パラメータの局所位数を整数として定める。系 2.2(ii) の証明では剰余次数と剰余標数の対数を重みとして、その局所位数の和を取る。高さの有限部分との等式は、参照 Lean 実装の Height.lean 第 582 行にある。
